text: Caldera's 5,000 inverters each send a reading every few minutes. This video wires up the stream and Lambda that catch every one of them and land it, untouched, in the raw data lake.
Three pieces, one job: the Kinesis stream catches the firehose, the ingest Lambda fires on every batch, and every reading lands in S3 exactly as it arrived, partitioned by date.
The handler is deliberately simple: decode each record, parse the JSON, write it straight to the raw bucket. No typing, no dedup -- that's a different job, built next lesson.
Kinesis and Lambda deliver at least once, so a retry can land the same reading twice. That's fine -- the raw lake is append-only, never treated as already clean.
Every reading is safely landing in raw. Next: cataloging it with a Glue Crawler and cleaning it with a real PySpark job.
